artifacts.summary: Five-phase, four-wave plan giving Gate 8 a three-way verdict branch (pass / warn_advisory / fail) driven by run-all.sh's existing --fail-on-new accounting; states the chosen all-expected semantics (exits zero, distinguishable on three channels) and justifies it against six consumers, four named in the dispatch plus the gate cache and the zero-check-under-filter branch.

memory_candidates.content: When changing the SEVERITY of a verify-deploy.sh gate's verdict (fail -> warn_advisory, or either -> pass), the consumer set to re-verify is larger than the deploy_findings_snapshot callers a task description typically names. Two further consumers read the verdict's severity side effects rather than its FINDING lines: (1) the --skip-unchanged gate cache -- pass() makes a gate cache-write-ELIGIBLE while fail()/warn()/warn_advisory() all append to GATE_DIRTY_LIST and invalidate, so demoting a failing gate to pass() silently caches a warm PASS over a genuinely failing corpus; (2) the zero-check-under-filter branch -- a --only-gate N selection whose every named gate SKIPs produces CHECKS=0 and exit 2 ('the run attested to nothing'), so a severity change that stops incrementing CHECKS converts a real verdict into an exit-2 error. warn_advisory() is the only non-blocking primitive that preserves both (increments CHECKS, appends to GATE_DIRTY_LIST), which is why it, not pass(), is the correct instrument for 'visible but never batch-blocking'.
